text:
jess_support: Escalation from Acme — they upgraded to @redwoodai/sdk JS v0.9.2 and their rerank outputs look broken. They expect numeric scores but are getting strings like "0.00" and sorting behaves oddly. Posting thread and repro below.

acme_dev (via DM to support): "We call client.rerank({query, candidates}) and expect an array of numbers in resp.scores. After the upgrade most scores are "0.00" strings and our sort orders are wrong. Reverting to 0.9.1 fixes it." :frowning:

jess_support: Their minimal repro code (TS):
```ts
import Redwood from '@redwoodai/sdk';
const client = new Redwood({key: process.env.RW});
const resp = await client.rerank({
  query: 'best restaurant',
  candidates: ['Italian bistro', 'sushi bar', 'burger joint']
});
console.log(resp);
```

What they *see* in their console: 
```json
{"candidates":["Italian bistro","sushi bar","burger joint"],"scores":["0.00","0.00","0.00"]}
```

But server-side logs and a curl call show numeric scores: 
```json
{"candidates":["Italian bistro","sushi bar","burger joint"],"scores":[0.913245,0.4032,0.29911]}
```

jess_support: So network payload from API is correct, SDK appears to be transforming scores into strings. Customer included Node v18.15.0 and Content-Type: application/json.

sarah_sdklib: Thanks. Can you confirm whether the SDK does any response post-processing? I recently added a UI-friendly formatting helper for scores in v0.9.2 but I thought it was opt-in. Tagging @mike_eng to triage.

mike_eng: I repro locally. curl -> numbers. SDK (v0.9.2) -> strings. Bisected to commit ab12f2 and to a new util formatScores in client/lib/format.ts. Current implementation: 
```ts
export function formatScores(arr: number[]) {
  return arr.map(s => s.toFixed(2));
}
```
Then the response handling does: 
```ts
const body = await res.json();
body.scores = formatScores(body.scores); // mutates canonical response
return body;
```
That turns numbers into strings (toFixed returns string). We also didn't change the TypeScript types so code compiled but broke runtime semantics.

sarah_sdklib: Ok that's the bug. We should never mutate the canonical response. That breaks numeric operations in downstream code (sorting, thresholds).

jess_support: Customer asked for a quick workaround they can use today.

mike_eng: Short-term workaround for customers: coerce back to numbers: resp.scores = resp.scores.map(Number) or resp.scores.map(parseFloat). Not great but works. Longer term: ship patch. I'll prepare a hotfix.

linus_ml: Also check Python SDK for the same pattern. I remember a recent pretty-print helper landed in py-sdk too. If both SDKs format scores globally we'll need coordinated releases and a customer advisory.

sarah_sdklib: I'll open an internal issue and draft PR. Proposed fix: change formatScores to return number[] if used for canonical response, and expose a separate prettyFormatScores that returns strings for UI. Better: never overwrite response.scores; instead add body._pretty_scores for UI. Add unit tests asserting typeof body.scores[0] === 'number'.

mike_eng: creating hotfix branch hotfix/sdk-preserve-scores, updating code to: 
```diff
- body.scores = formatScores(body.scores);
+ const pretty = prettyFormatScores(body.scores);
+ body._pretty_scores = pretty; // do not mutate numeric scores
```
Will run unit + integration tests. If green, cut v0.9.3.

jess_support: I've informed Acme about a workaround and that a patch will be released soon. They want ETA.

mike_eng: If CI is green, I can cut and publish v0.9.3 in ~90 minutes. I'll also scan error telemetry to see how many customers might be affected.

deploy_bot: CI triggered for branch hotfix/sdk-preserve-scores (job #4857).

linus_ml: Good. Also include in the changelog a note to search customer repos for uses of resp.scores.sort or arithmetic; string values can silently break logic. Recommend customers pinning at <=0.9.1 until they upgrade.

sarah_sdklib: Drafted PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/347 — fixes, tests, changelog entry. Diff excerpt: 
```diff
- body.scores = formatScores(body.scores);
+ const pretty = prettyFormatScores(body.scores);
+ body._pretty_scores = pretty;
```
Added test: rerank_response_preserves_number_types -> expect(typeof resp.scores[0]).toBe('number').

jess_support: Sending customer update now with workaround and ETA. Template: 
---
Hi — we found a bug in JS SDK v0.9.2 that converts rerank scores into formatted strings. Short-term: coerce with resp.scores = resp.scores.map(Number). We're releasing v0.9.3 with a fix (preserves numeric scores) in ~90 minutes. We'll follow up when release is live and confirm your repro works. Sorry for the trouble.
---

mike_eng: CI passed, cutting v0.9.3 release now and will publish to npm. Will also run their repro against published package and post results.

deploy_bot: Release job queued: release/sdk-js/v0.9.3 (#347).

jess_support: Thanks everyone. I'll close the escalation after Acme confirms. Follow-ups: check py-sdk, add customer advisory for those who upgraded to 0.9.2, and run telemetry scan for rerank consumers. :thumbsup:

(END)
